Confirmed misconception: Believes SUM(x) OVER (ORDER BY y) returns the grand total on every row, not knowing that ORDER BY inside OVER produces a running total in which tied rows share a value. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes BFS finds shortest paths in weighted graphs, equating the route with the fewest edges with the route of least total weight. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Does not know that an in-order traversal of a valid BST visits keys in sorted order; believes it returns keys in insertion order or level order. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes a hash table stores its keys in sorted order, so iterating over it yields keys sorted and it can produce ordered output or the smallest key without extra sorting. Suspected (insufficient corroboration) misconception: Believes the BST property only requires each node to be greater than its left child and smaller than its right child, rather than greater than every key in its left subtree and smaller than every key in its right subtree.
